original_question: Determine the border subrank of a generic tensor, and characterize conditions under which a tensor has border subrank strictly higher than the generic value.
target_in_paper: Section 4.2, Problem 22: "Determine the border subrank of a generic tensor and give conditions for a tensor to have border subrank higher than the generic one." ([agates.mimuw.edu.pl](https://agates.mimuw.edu.pl/images/notes_and_reports/Gesmundo_Geometry_of_Tensors_Open_Problems_and_Research_Directions.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the exact target almost verbatim: it asks for the border subrank of a generic tensor and for a characterization of tensors whose border subrank exceeds the generic value. It also stays in the paper's tensor-subrank setting rather than drifting to neighboring problems about upper-bound methods or other tensor ranks. ([agates.mimuw.edu.pl](https://agates.mimuw.edu.pl/images/notes_and_reports/Gesmundo_Geometry_of_Tensors_Open_Problems_and_Research_Directions.pdf))
missing_details: The ambient field should be stated explicitly: the paper's default setting is over the complex numbers. ([agates.mimuw.edu.pl](https://agates.mimuw.edu.pl/images/notes_and_reports/Gesmundo_Geometry_of_Tensors_Open_Problems_and_Research_Directions.pdf))

You need to fix a tensor format V_1⊗···⊗V_d; the phrase "generic tensor" and the resulting generic value are only meaningful relative to a fixed tensor space. The nearby discussion especially highlights the equal-dimension case T∈C^n⊗···⊗C^n. ([agates.mimuw.edu.pl](https://agates.mimuw.edu.pl/images/notes_and_reports/Gesmundo_Geometry_of_Tensors_Open_Problems_and_Research_Directions.pdf))

Border subrank must be defined explicitly as Q̄(T)=max{q:T degenerates to u_d(q)}. ([agates.mimuw.edu.pl](https://agates.mimuw.edu.pl/images/notes_and_reports/Gesmundo_Geometry_of_Tensors_Open_Problems_and_Research_Directions.pdf))

The unit tensor must be defined: u_d(q)=Σ_{i=1}^q e_i⊗···⊗e_i∈(C^q)^{⊗ d}. ([agates.mimuw.edu.pl](https://agates.mimuw.edu.pl/images/notes_and_reports/Gesmundo_Geometry_of_Tensors_Open_Problems_and_Research_Directions.pdf))

The notion of degeneration must be specified via the End(V_1)×···×End(V_d)-action, with the paper also noting the equivalent GL(V_1)×···×GL(V_d) orbit-closure formulation after re-embedding into a common tensor space. ([agates.mimuw.edu.pl](https://agates.mimuw.edu.pl/images/notes_and_reports/Gesmundo_Geometry_of_Tensors_Open_Problems_and_Research_Directions.pdf))
To make the question fully stand-alone, say that "generic" means a Zariski-general tensor in the chosen format.

The second clause should explicitly mean "strictly larger than the border subrank attained by a generic tensor in the same fixed format," so that the comparison value is unambiguous. ([agates.mimuw.edu.pl](https://agates.mimuw.edu.pl/images/notes_and_reports/Gesmundo_Geometry_of_Tensors_Open_Problems_and_Research_Directions.pdf))

There are no homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency hypotheses in the paper's formulation; adding any such restrictions would move away from the target problem. ([agates.mimuw.edu.pl](https://agates.mimuw.edu.pl/images/notes_and_reports/Gesmundo_Geometry_of_Tensors_Open_Problems_and_Research_Directions.pdf))
refined_question: Fix complex vector spaces V_1,…,V_d and a tensor space V_1⊗···⊗V_d. For T∈V_1⊗···⊗V_d, let u_d(q)=Σ_{i=1}^q e_i⊗···⊗e_i∈(C^q)^{⊗ d}, and define the border subrank by Q̄(T)=max{q:T degenerates to u_d(q)}, where degeneration is taken with respect to the End(V_1)×···×End(V_d)-action after re-embedding into a common tensor space. Determine the value of Q̄(T) for a Zariski-generic tensor T in this fixed format, and characterize the tensors in the same format for which Q̄(T) is strictly larger than the generic value Q̄_gen of that format. ([agates.mimuw.edu.pl](https://agates.mimuw.edu.pl/images/notes_and_reports/Gesmundo_Geometry_of_Tensors_Open_Problems_and_Research_Directions.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for a fixed complex tensor format V_1⊗···⊗V_d, determine for a Zariski-generic tensor T the largest q such that the unit tensor u_d(q) lies in the GL(V_1)×···×GL(V_d)-orbit closure of T (after re-embedding into a common tensor space), and characterize the tensors whose orbit-closures contain some u_d(q') with q'>Q̄_gen. ([agates.mimuw.edu.pl](https://agates.mimuw.edu.pl/images/notes_and_reports/Gesmundo_Geometry_of_Tensors_Open_Problems_and_Research_Directions.pdf))
justification: The draft is an almost exact paraphrase of Problem 22, so this is the nearest official formulation in the paper. The surrounding context immediately supplies the hidden assumptions needed to make it stand-alone: the paper works over complex numbers; restriction and degeneration are defined via the End(V_1)×···×End(V_d)-action, with degeneration identified with GL(V_1)×···×GL(V_d)-orbit closure; the unit tensor u_d(q) is defined just before the section; and border subrank is then defined as Q̄(T)=max{q:T degenerates to u_d(q)}. The paragraph immediately preceding Problem 22 also explains the local scope motivating the question by discussing generic tensors, especially T∈C^n⊗···⊗C^n, and noting that the generic border subrank is still unknown, while an upper bound Q̄(T)≤n−1 is known in that equal-dimension setting. No homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency conditions belong to this target problem. ([agates.mimuw.edu.pl](https://agates.mimuw.edu.pl/images/notes_and_reports/Gesmundo_Geometry_of_Tensors_Open_Problems_and_Research_Directions.pdf))
